subject: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions

Hi Lucy —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can put together a tailored pricing estimate and PoC plan: 

- Token volumes: could you confirm expected monthly token volume (best estimate and 90th percentile peak)?
- Budget: ballpark monthly budget range you have in mind for hosting inference (so we can optimize for cost/perf).
- Unit economics target: any target $/1M tokens you’re aiming for?
- Workload patterns: typical request sizes (tokens per call), percent of streaming/chat vs. non-streaming, and expected concurrency/peak RPS.

From what we discussed, a couple of notes: continuous-batching-friendly workloads (many short, frequent requests across many users) often see significant unit-cost reductions versus single-request serving. If you expect a high degree of continuous batching we can model a lower $/1M token number in the estimate.

I attached a rough pricing template (redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx) and will update it once you confirm volumes/budget. Proposed next steps: you share the numbers, we run a short 2-week PoC with continuous batching enabled on a small shard, and present the measured unit economics.

Would love your answers to the bullets above — if easier, feel free to reply with short bullets.

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx

From: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the recap — answers below (short bullets as requested):

- Monthly tokens: baseline ~50M tokens/month; 90th percentile (peak) monthly could be ~80–100M during campaigns.
- Typical tokens per request: median 120 tokens, 90th pct ~450 tokens. We have a mix of short chat replies (30–80 tokens) and longer generation tasks.
- Workload shape: ~70% streaming/chat-style small replies (frequent), ~30% longer generative calls. The streaming ones are continuous across many users — we expect continuous batching to be effective.
- Peak concurrency: average steady-state concurrency ~3–4 rps; peak ~6–8 rps for short periods.
- Budget: rough budget range $6k–$9k/month to start, could expand if unit economics are favorable.
- Target unit economics: ideally ~$1,200–$1,800 per 1M tokens (we’re flexible but want to understand realistic numbers).

Happy to share a sample production traffic export — I attached a short summary (acme_prod_summary.pdf). Let me know if you want raw logs.

Best,
Lucy
Head of Product, Acme Corp
lucy.chen@acme.com

Attachment: acme_prod_summary.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions

Lucy — great, thanks for the detail — super helpful. A few immediate thoughts and proposed next steps: 

- Given the 70% streaming and the median request size (~120 tokens), continuous batching should give a meaningful reduction in per-token inference cost compared to treating each request individually. For a conservative model we’d expect ~20–35% cost savings with continuous batching plus prefix/KV caching; more aggressive tuning (larger batching windows, relaxed latency SLOs) could push savings higher.
- With your baseline ~50M tokens/month and peak behavior, we can model 1M-token unit costs in the ballpark of $1,100–$1,600 depending on the batching aggressiveness and quantization choices. That aligns with your $1,200–$1,800 target on the conservative side.
- Concurrency: the steady-state 3–4 rps is ideal for continuous batching. Peak spikes to 6–8 rps are manageable with autoscaling + short burst capacity; we’ll model a safety buffer in the estimate.

Next steps: 
1) We’ll prepare two pricing scenarios in the attached updated estimate: conservative (lower batching, tighter latency) and aggressive (larger batching windows, prioritized cost savings).
2) Run a 2-week PoC on a small shard with continuous batching enabled and metrics instrumented (latency P50/P95, tokens served, batching efficiency).
3) Weekly sync while PoC runs + a final review demo.

If that sounds good I’ll (a) update the spreadsheet and share an annotated version, (b) send an invite for a 30-minute kickoff (link: https://calendly.com/marissa-cole/redwood-demo), and (c) scope the PoC success criteria.

Attachment: next_steps.md

Thanks — looking forward to this.
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-06T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up: batching & concurrency assumptions

(Internal) Quick action items for us — copying here so it’s in-thread: 

- Camila: please prepare the two pricing scenarios (conservative vs aggressive) in the spreadsheet; include assumptions for batching window sizes (50ms, 250ms, 500ms), quantization levels, and expected batching efficiency numbers.
- Aditya: can you prepare a short PoC runbook (2-week) with instrumentation hooks: tokens/time, batching window distribution, cache hit rate, latency P50/P95, and autoscaling thresholds. Also include estimated infra cost for a small shard.
- Marissa: I’ll own kickoff with Lucy and confirm PoC success criteria & permissions for sampling logs.

We’ll aim to send the updated estimate and PoC runbook by EOD Friday.

-Marissa
